title: Consolidate node health probes and simplify GPU drain/repair orchestration
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem:
Over the past 18 months we accumulated multiple ad-hoc node health checks, duplicate probes, and separate evacuation flows for drains, repairs, and orphaned GPU allocations. This duplication causes: increased load on the capacity planner, spurious node churn during upgrades, race conditions between the lease reconciler and the drain controller, and confusion in incident playbooks.

Goal:
Consolidate health probes into a single lightweight node-status aggregator, centralize decision logic for drain vs repair vs reclaim, and simplify the orchestration so the capacity planner sees a single, well-defined lifecycle signal per node. The work should reduce planner GC churn by ~30% and improve mean time to stable allocation after node repair/upgrade windows.

Scope (what we will change):
- Introduce node-status-aggregator service (binary) that subscribes to existing kube/probe events and outputs canonical node lifecycle events (READY, DEGRADED, DRAINING, REPAIRING, ORPHANED).
- Replace two in-repo ad-hoc probes with a single probe shim that reports to the aggregator.
- Refactor the capacity planner to consume the aggregator's canonical events instead of raw probe blobs; remove planner-side heuristics for drain/repair race resolution.
- Simplify lease reconciliation by making the lease-controller authoritative for active allocations; have aggregator emit a reconciliation fence when node enters REPAIRING.
- Add migration shim to translate historical signals for a 4-week grace period while rollout completes.

Non-goals:
- Rewriting the entire autoscaler state machine. We intentionally keep the planner's high-level architecture intact and only change input signals and a small reconciliation surface.

Success metrics:
- 30% reduction in capacity planner reconcile loops per minute on average across clusters.
- 20% reduction in tokenized allocation failures related to node-state races.
- No customer-facing request latencies increase above 1% during rollout.

Design trade-offs considered:
- Central aggregator vs. lightweight distributed consensus: chosen central aggregator reduces duplication and makes debugging easier, at the cost of an extra process. Aggregator will be HA (2 pods) and stateless for failover.
- Aggressive immediate reclamation vs. conservative fence windows: we pick a conservative fence (30s) to avoid premature reclaim and customer impact during upgrades.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature-flagged deploy of aggregator in staging reading from a kafka topic (non-authoritative) and writing canonical events to a new topic.
2) Backfill: run translator shim in planner to log decisions for 1 week while comparing outputs.
3) Canary: enable planner consumer in a small dev cluster and run dual-path reconciliation (old logic + aggregator) for 48h.
4) Gradual switch: flip planner to authoritative aggregator input across 10% -> 50% -> 100% of clusters with health gates.
5) Deprecate old probe code and remove after 4-week grace period.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for aggregator translation rules and fence windows.
- Integration test harness simulating node flapping, long repairs, and concurrent drains.
- Load test to validate planner reconcile rate improvements and to ensure no regression for burst traffic.
- New dashboards: planner-reconciles/min, node-event-latency, allocation-failure-by-cause.

Backout plan:
- Rollback to previous planner consumer (we keep old topic and blackhole aggregator input) and revert feature flag. The planner will continue to accept legacy signals until full rollback completes.

Observability changes:
- Emit tracing spans: node-aggregator.process -> planner.consume so latency traces show end-to-end.
- Add tags for event_source, node_pool, and fence_id.
- Dashboards and alerts in Console: one new SLO check for planner-reconcile-rate regression.

Notes and links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Node+Status+Aggregator+Design
- Proto for canonical events: https://git.redwood.ai/infr/protos/merge_requests/219
- Related infra PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infrctl/pull/2145
